p: It is stated in the Gemara (Pesachim 68b):
It is the day on which the Torah was given."
in light of what is written
that on Purim, when there was a rescue of lives and bodies,
which they sought to destroy and kill,
they established rejoicing and feasting for the body;
when there was a rescue from forced apostasy,
הִיא רַק שִׂמְחָה לַנֶּפֶשׁ וְלֹא לַגּוּף.
it is only a rejoicing for the soul and not for the body.
So how is the reason to be understood,
that because the Torah was given on it
that one should rejoice on it with food and drink
to show that it is pleasing and accepted —
the day on which the Torah was given.
if he were rejoicing of his own accord;
but since there is a mitzvah in it,
there is in it no indication or proof
that it is pleasing and accepted by him,
since he is compelled to fulfill the mitzvah.
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
But the matter rests on what they said:
הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּשַׁבָּת דִּבְעִינַן נַמִּי לָכֶם,
"All agree regarding Shabbos that we also require 'for you,'"
דִּכְתִיב וְקָרָאתָ לַשַּׁבָּת עוֹנֶג (יְשַׁעְיָה נח, יג).
since it is written, "And you shall call the Shabbos a delight" (Yeshayah 58:13).
"a soul in which there is all perfection,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב פח, ב),
when the rectification will be complete,
so that one will no longer feel bodily pleasure.
And the mitzvah is "And you shall call the Shabbos a delight":
that he should delight only the neshamah yeseirah,
and takes delight in the delights of Shabbos,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב רד, ב).
as written (in the holy Zohar, Zohar II 204b).
in analyzing the wording of the Gemara:
and they did not say "one who takes delight on Shabbos"
or "one who delights himself on Shabbos."
that even eating for bodily pleasure on Shabbos
מִכָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁבַח הַמְעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
nevertheless the praise of "one who delights the Shabbos"
applies only when he intends it for the sake of Heaven,
and this is "And you shall call the Shabbos a delight."
And "all agree that we require 'for you'"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁהַלָּכֶם הוּא גַּם כֵּן בִּקְדוּשָּׁה.
means that the "for you" is also in holiness.
the meal is called "the feast of the King,"
as it is written, "My bread for My fire-offerings" (Bamidbar 28:2),
כָּל שְׂאוֹר וְכָל דְּבַשׁ לֹא תַקְרִיבוּ (וַיִּקְרָא ב, יא),
"any leaven and any honey you shall not offer" (Vayikra 2:11),
since there is still the leaven in the dough,
so that one might intend his own pleasure;
therefore it is forbidden to offer chametz.
as it is stated in the holy Zohar
(אֱמוֹר, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג צז, ב, בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא):
"And with the offering of the Omer
which fled from the Eishes Chayil," etc.;
וּבְגִין כָּךְ אִקְרֵי בְּגַוְונָא דָא עֲצֶרֶת
"and therefore it is called in this manner 'Atzeres,'
for it contains the nullification of the yetzer hara.
וְעַל דָּא לָא כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ חַטָּאת
Therefore 'chatas' is not written regarding it,
דִּכְתִיב חַטָּאת לַה׳ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כח, טו) וְכוּלֵּי.
where it is written 'a chatas to Hashem' (Bamidbar 28:15)," etc.
That is, at the time of Mattan Torah it is written,
אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי אֱלֹהִים אַתֶּם (תְּהִלִּים פב, ו),
meaning that they would not have died
the entire blemish of the serpent,
and since the Angel of Death was nullified,
the yetzer hara was nullified too,
for he is the Angel of Death
And so it is stated in the Midrash
(שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א, ב, פָּרָשַׁת יִשָּׁקֵנִי):
בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁשָּׁמְעוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ
"When Yisrael heard 'You shall have no other gods,'
the yetzer hara was uprooted from their heart."
the yetzer hara returned to its place,
the holiness of this time is aroused,
which is the nullification of the leaven in the dough.
And what remains is only from the fact
that leaven is one of the three things
of which "a large amount is harmful and a small amount is good"
That is, the part that is needed,
and of it some will remain even in the future,
תּוֹלְדוֹת, זֹהַר חֵלֶק א קלח, א):
"For were it not for the yetzer hara,
there would be no joy of Torah learning."
which is the "small amount that is good" that remains.
And this is the matter of the dispute of
רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּכָל יוֹם טוֹב:
Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua regarding every Yom Tov:
אוֹ כּוּלּוֹ לַה׳ אוֹ כּוּלּוֹ לָכֶם,
either entirely for Hashem or entirely for you;
that is, one who is able
also be for the sake of Heaven,
so that he will not feel self-gratification —
then it is entirely for you.
And one who cannot direct his intent
for him it shall be entirely for Hashem.
For certainly the meaning is not
that the choice is in his hands to choose
that every one of Yisrael is able
to eat on Yom Tov in holiness,
and the Torah simply said to divide it:
half for Hashem and half for you.
to have his bodily pleasure be in holiness,
for then the light is revealed
from the time of the giving of our Torah,
when the leaven in the dough was nullified,
And this is what they said:
הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בַּעֲצֶרֶת דִּבְעִינַן נַמִּי לָכֶם,
"All agree regarding Atzeres that we also require 'for you'" —
that the "for you" also be in holiness;
It is the day on which the Torah was given,"
and this is aroused every year,
so that one can nullify the leaven in the dough
and the "for you" too will be in holiness.
